svg.title: Two symmetric normal quantiles recover the mean and a positive standard deviation
svg.desc: The tenth percentile of X is forty and the ninetieth percentile is sixty. Symmetry puts the mean at fifty. The unrounded standard normal ninetieth percentile is about one point two eight one five five one five six six, giving standard deviation about seven point eight zero three zero four one four six one. Using the explicitly supplied three-decimal scores minus one point two eight two and plus one point two eight two gives the approximate equations forty equals approximately mu minus one point two eight two sigma and sixty equals approximately mu plus one point two eight two sigma. They give standard deviation about seven point eight zero zero three one two zero one two. Both methods round to seven point eight zero to two decimal places. The diagram uses the unrounded fitted curve and shades the interval between the two supplied quantiles. Positive spread requires increasing quantile values as cumulative probability increases.
